events.what: Explicit degree-23 polynomial over Q with Galois group M23, completing realization of all 26 sporadic simple groups over Q
events.ai_basis: We used Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 4.8, and ChatGPT 5.6 Sol for searching the literature, code generation, testing hypotheses, ruling out other approaches, devising computational strategies, checking our results, and proofreading our manuscript. ... Our final results were verified in Magma and PARI/GP without the use of AI.

judgement.doubts: One finite group (M23) is a case of 'every finite group', so partial is right regardless of verification; the explicit polynomial is checkable by computer algebra. The AI role is the borderline call. The paper's disclosure lists literature search, code generation, hypothesis testing, strategy suggestions, checking and proofreading, and none of these is AI-produced mathematics in the result. But the co-author blog says AI produced initial numerical approximations of the Belyi map data that were later recognised via PSLQ. If those approximations fed the final coefficients, 'assisted' could be defended. The same blog and the record's competing_reading say the decisive coordinate switch was human, and the record does not show whether the AI-made numerics survived into the final polynomial. I keep the human reviewer's 'none', with medium confidence. Epoch AI calling the AI 'instrumental' is a characterisation by a third party, not the authors' account of what the model produced.
